artworks.title: The Circle of the Thieves; Buoso Donati Attacked by the Serpent
artworks.description: The image shows four figures standing within an abstract environment. The first figure on the left is holding their hands up and wearing a robe. The second figure behind the first wears similar attire. The third and fourth figures, nude males with muscular bodies, appear to be reacting to something in the scene. The setting includes stylized clouds and a landscape with flame-like or pointed formations. A serpentine creature emerges between the third and fourth figures. The background is highly stylized with swirling patterns and jagged lines.

artworks.title: The Circle of the Falsifiers: Dante and Virgil Covering their Noses because of the stench
artworks.description: This is a drawing featuring tortured figures and mountainous landscapes. The foreground shows figures in distress or anguish, engaged in struggle. Two tall, robed figures stand on a rocky outcrop overseeing the scene below. The background shows ominous clouds and distant mountains, creating a sense of despair. The composition is detailed and conveys intense emotions related to suffering and conflict.

artworks.title: The Circle of the Traitors; Dante's Foot Striking Bocca degli Abbate
artworks.description: A drawing of two robed figures standing near a body of water with faces visible beneath the surface. The scene is in a monochromatic style, with the central figures draped in flowing garments by the water, filled with faces of individuals. Some faces are partially submerged, showing expressions of distress or contemplation. The foreground displays detailed faces, creating a mood and narrative. In the background, a rocky cliff with carved faces adds to the mystical atmosphere. The composition blends human forms with natural elements, creating a surreal quality. The drawing's style suggests a symbolic or allegorical theme, focusing on the interaction between the figures and their environment in this ethereal landscape.

artworks.title: The Circle of the Lustful: Paolo and Francesca
artworks.description: This is a drawing of swirling figures and celestial imagery, featuring a large spiral composed of intertwined figures, a cloaked figure next to a reclining form, and another form encircled by light above. The composition is filled with intricate detailing, creating a sense of motion and interaction. The style is reminiscent of works inspired by the Romantic period.

artworks.title: The Circle of the Lustful: Paolo and Francesca
artworks.description: This is a drawing of swirling figures. The scene depicts a spiral of figures flowing together. There is a sense of motion and interaction among them. On one side, a robed figure gazes upon a reclining figure on the ground. The composition is detailed, with flowing lines creating movement and energy. Shading and line work create depth and texture in this monochromatic work.

artworks.title: Sketch of a Swordsman Standing Over His Defeated Opponent [recto]
artworks.description: This is a drawing of figures and potential structures sketched with light pencil lines. The composition includes several indistinct human forms positioned amid architectural elements, suggested by faint lines resembling structures or columns. The figures are roughly outlined and carry a sense of movement, especially the central figure in stride. The overall impression is of an unfinished study or preparatory sketch, with each line delicate and suggestive rather than definitive.

artworks.title: Sketch of a Swordsman Standing Over His Defeated Opponent [verso]
artworks.description: The image shows several abstract figures in long flowing garments. The figures are loosely defined and appear to be standing or possibly interacting in a group. The elongated forms are outlined in thin, soft pencil strokes, giving the piece an ethereal and unfinished quality. The clothing forms graceful lines that suggest movement. The use of shading is minimal, emphasizing the shapes' contour and form rather than details.

artworks.title: Winter
artworks.artist: Pieter van der Heyden after Hans Bol
artworks.description: The image is viewed from a slightly elevated angle, showing a bustling scene. In the distance, there are hills, a waterway with small boats, and a large fortified building surrounded by activity. The detailed engraving features fine and meticulous lines, depicting textures and patterns. The monochromatic color palette focuses on brown tones against the paper, creating depth. The scene includes architectural details, figures, and winter activities, with trees in the sky.

artworks.title: Croix de Moulin-les-Planches
artworks.description: The image shows a stone cross in the foreground, surrounded by buildings and trees. People are gathered around the base of the cross. The buildings are rustic with stone and wooden elements, with smoke rising from one structure. The artwork features fine brushstrokes, creating a textured appearance. The color palette is monochromatic, using grayscale shades. Trees and distant structures can be seen in the background, with a lightly clouded sky.

artworks.title: Charles Lameth
artworks.medium: etching, stipple and roulette on laid paper
artworks.description: The image features the upper body of a man in profile, facing right. The man has a sharp nose and prominent cheekbones, with composed expression. His hair is styled traditionally in the 18th century, powdered and tied back. He wears a formal coat with buttons, a high-collared shirt, and a cravat. There is no visible jewelry or objects in hand. The background is a textured oval set against a blank space. The text below identifies him as Charles Lameth, a deputy to the National Assembly in 1789, with publisher information at the bottom.

artworks.title: Pheasant and Cattail (Faisan et roseau)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a bird with long tail feathers and a cattail plant. The drawing is created with intricate, fine lines, capturing the delicate form of the bird which seems to be in motion, its tail elegantly trailing behind it. The bird's plumage is detailed with various patterns, and its neck appears to be gracefully arched. Below the bird, a faint outline of a cattail plant is visible, with its slender stalk and elongated leaves rendered with minimalistic strokes. The background is plain, allowing the focus to remain on the bird and plant. A small red seal is present near the bottom of the drawing.

artworks.title: The Road Leading to Bellevue (Le Chemin montant à Bellevue)
artworks.description: The image shows a landscape view with a high horizon. Treetops and some structures are visible in the distance. The drawing uses intricate etching techniques to depict trees and foliage. The color palette is limited to monochrome tones of black and white. Closest to us is an open area transitioning into densely packed trees depicted with curved lines. Further back, a cluster of trees extends towards the horizon, with hints of buildings interspersed throughout.

artworks.title: Trembles au bord de la Seine (Aspens on the Banks of the Seine)
artworks.medium: etching and drypoint on laid paper
artworks.description: The image depicts a view from a slightly off-center position on a calm bank, looking through a sparse row of tall, slender trees towards a body of water. The horizon is low, with subtle outlines of trees and shrubbery in the distance on the opposite bank. The artwork uses fine pen strokes with a cross-hatching technique to create texture. The color palette is monochrome, with sepia tones giving a warm, vintage feel. A small boat is tucked close to the trees, partly concealed by underbrush.

artworks.title: Untitled (The Dream of the Mogul?)
artworks.description: This is a painting of amorphous dark forms, a serpent, and abstract humanoid figures in a mysterious landscape. The scene is dominated by a serpentine creature in the foreground, with shadowy shapes in the background suggesting cliffs or ancient ruins. Elements of surrealism are present, with figures and shapes that are partially defined, creating a dreamlike setting. Monochrome tones enhance the mood of the scene. This painting is in the style of Gustave Moreau.

artworks.title: Euntes in Emaus (The Pilgrims to Emmaus)
artworks.artist: Johannes and Lucas van Doetechum after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.dimensions: sheet (trimmed to plate mark): 32.4 x 42.7 cm (12 3/4 x 16 13/16 in.)
artworks.description: The image shows a landscape viewed from an elevated perspective. The horizon features mountains, a setting sun, and a sky filled with wispy cloud formations. The composition is detailed with line work. Three figures walk along a path lined with trees in the foreground. Beyond them is a pastoral scene with boats on a river, livestock, cottages, and greenery. In the far distance, a fortified structure is seen on a hill overlooking the river. The image is in black and white, focusing on shading and contrast to create a visually engaging scene.

artworks.title: Milites Requiescentes (Soldiers at Rest)
artworks.artist: Johannes and Lucas van Doetechum after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.dimensions: sheet (trimmed to plate mark): 33.1 x 42.7 cm (13 1/16 x 16 13/16 in.)
artworks.description: The image shows a landscape view from an elevated position, overlooking a village and countryside. Distant mountains are visible on the horizon under a sky with clouds. A large tree with detailed branches spans the left to the right of the image. Two figures are resting by a pathway that leads through the scene towards the village. In the distance, a rocky outcrop with a castle can be seen. The style of the image features fine lines, giving intricate details, depth, and a textured look. The color palette is monochromatic, possibly in sepia tones or greyscale, conveying light and shadow and creating a timeless atmosphere.

artworks.title: The Big Fish Eat the Little Fish
artworks.artist: Pieter van der Heyden after Pieter Bruegel the Elder (after Hieronymus Bosch?)
artworks.dimensions: sheet (trimmed within plate mark): 21.1 x 29.7 cm (8 5/16 x 11 11/16 in.)
artworks.description: Printed with fine black lines on light tan paper, a whale-sized fish spilling smaller fish from its gaping mouth and a gash in its belly fills a beach in this horizontal engraving. The fish lies on its side with its belly facing us, and one bulging eye peers off to our right. A man wearing a helmet holds a knife twice his own size with the blade up as he cuts the fish’s belly. Fish and scallop shells of all sizes tumble from its cavernous mouth and side. Several fish also have smaller fish in their mouths. On the far side of the fish, a man stands on a ladder braced against the enormous creature, holding a raised trident as he looks down, his face covered by the wide brim of his hat. On the land to our left is another smaller fish with human legs, which carries a fish in its mouth. It passes a man who carries a fish on his back outside a dilapidated cottage as he climbs a ladder leaning against a tree. Two other fish hang from the tree’s branches. Around the shoreline to the right, fish surface with more fish in their mouths. A man and a boy wearing tunics and long headdresses sit in a rowboat close to us, pointing as a second man in the boat holds a knife in his teeth and pulls a small fish from the body of a larger one. Another man sits on the beach further up the shoreline, about to catch a fish using fish as bait. The water stretches back to a town in the far distance. Boats float in the middle distance and some approach another whale-sized fish beached on a small island behind a tall rocky outcropping. About a dozen people with spears gather on the island around that fish. A flock of birds fly in silhouette in the distance beyond the island. A flying creature closer to us has a scaly body, gaping mouth, wavy tail, and tear-drop shaped wings. The print is inscribed in the lower left, “Hieronijmus.Bos. inuentor” and in the lower center, “ECCE.” The lower right is inscribed, “COCK. EXCV. 1557.”

artworks.title: The Big Fish Eat the Little Fish
artworks.artist: Hendrik Hondius after Pieter Bruegel the Elder (after Hieronymus Bosch?
artworks.description: Printed with fine black lines on light tan paper, a whale-sized fish spilling smaller fish from its gaping mouth and a gash in its belly fills a beach in this horizontal engraving. The fish lies on its side with its belly facing us, and one bulging eye peers off to our left. A man wearing a helmet holds a knife twice his own size with the blade up as he cuts the fish’s belly. Fish and scallop shells of all sizes tumble from its cavernous mouth and side. Several fish also have smaller fish in their mouths. On the far side of the fish, a man stands on a ladder braced against the enormous creature, holding a raised trident as he looks down, his face covered by the wide brim of his hat. On the land to our right is another smaller fish with human legs, which carries a fish in its mouth. It passes a man who carries a fish on his back outside a dilapidated cottage as he climbs a ladder leaning against a tree. Two other fish hang from the tree’s branches. Around the shoreline to the left, fish surface with more fish in their mouths. A man and a boy wearing tunics and long headdresses sit in a rowboat close to us, pointing as a second man in the boat holds a knife in his teeth and pulls a small fish from the body of a larger one. The word “ECCE” is inscribe near the pointing man’s hand. Another man sits on the beach further up the shoreline, about to catch a fish using fish as bait. The water stretches back to a town in the far distance. Boats float in the middle distance and some approach another whale-sized fish beached on a small island behind a tall rocky outcropping. An inscription in the upper left corner reads, “Grandibus exigui sunt pisces piscibus esca.” The print is signed in the lower left corner, “CJVisscher excud,” with the CJV joined to make a monogram. An inscription printed in the margin under the image reads, “Siet sone dit heb’ick seer lange gheweten Dat die groote Vissen de cleyne eten. P. Breugel inven:.”

artworks.title: Christ and His Disciples on the Way to Emmaus
artworks.artist: Philip Galle after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: This artwork features three figures standing closely together in an outdoor setting. Each person faces slightly inward towards the center. The central figure has a halo around their head, and the other two individuals display concerned expressions. They are draped in long robes and carry staffs. One person wears a cap, knee-high shoes, and carries a small bag. The background consists of simple shaded lines indicating a landscape with subtle ground textures.

artworks.title: The Parable of the Wise and Foolish Virgins
artworks.artist: Philip Galle after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: This is a drawing featuring various figures, some with wings, merging with gothic architectural elements and clouds. Below, individuals engage in spinning and pouring olive oil, alluding to the parable of the Wise and Foolish Virgins. The upper section includes angelic figures and possibly wise or biblical figures engaged in a celestial court or gathering, complete with elaborate gothic window designs. Latin text scrolls enhance the narrative aspects of the drawing. Shadows and textures are intricately rendered, capturing depth and movement throughout the composition.

artworks.title: Peasants Fighting
artworks.artist: Anton Joseph Prenner after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.medium: etching and engraving on laid paper
artworks.description: This is a detailed drawing of a scene depicting several figures engaged in a tug-of-war. The foreground shows a dynamic struggle among the figures pulling against each other with tension. The figures are in motion, depicted with tense muscles and posture. The background features a rustic village setting with thatched-roof buildings and trees. Intricate cross-hatching and line work are used to create depth, shadow, and texture. Scattered papers on the ground contribute to the sense of activity and disorder in the scene. The style is similar to works by artists like Pieter Bruegel the Elder, known for detailed depictions of peasant life and lively scenes.

artworks.title: Magdalena Poenitens (The Penitent Magdalene)
artworks.artist: Johannes and Lucas van Doetechum after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.medium: etching and engraving on laid paper
artworks.description: The image features a mountainous landscape depicted in an intricate line-based style. The mountains spread across the upper part of the image, with a fortified structure nestled among them. A path winds through trees and rocks on the right, where a figure sits under a shelter. Further along the path, a person rides a horse. In the central area, a river flows through the valley with green patches and small buildings. The color scheme is monochromatic, accentuating detailed textures and creating a sense of depth.

artworks.title: Faith
artworks.artist: Philip Galle after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a religious scene in a church. The drawing shows a congregation of hooded and robed figures gathered around pillars and altars in a grand architectural space with Gothic structures such as tall, pointed arches. A podium is visible to the right, where someone seems to be speaking to the crowd. Religious artifacts and symbols, including a cross, are present. In the foreground, various objects like a ladder, scrolls, tools, and paraphernalia are scattered around. The intricate details and monochrome palette create a solemn atmosphere.

artworks.title: Hope
artworks.artist: Philip Galle after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a water scene with allegorical elements. Intricate details fill the scene with a castle-like structure in the background, partially engulfed by turbulent waves. The foreground shows tumultuous seas with large fish and a boat struggling against the current. A figure with a long, pointed hat stands amidst the waves, holding onto ropes tethered to two sea creatures. Nearby, figures are on small boats and appear to be in distress. Within the stone structures near the edge of the water, smaller figures are seen engaged in various activities. The cross-hatching and line work contribute to the textures of the water, stone, and characters, adding to the dynamic sense of movement and narrative drama depicted in the scene.
